question: What did a burst of gamma rays arriving 1.7 seconds after a gravitational wave reveal about the speed of gravity?
answer: That gravity travels at the speed of light, to within about one part in a thousand trillion. Both signals left two merging neutron stars some 130 million light-years away. A speed difference of one part in ten million would have opened a gap of about 13 years; the gap was under two seconds.
move: A tiny difference, carried far enough, grows large enough to measure.

diagram.caption: Speeds one part in ten million apart would mean 13 years; the gap was 1.7 seconds.

source: Abbott et al., Astrophysical Journal Letters, 2017
reference: Abbott et al., Gravitational Waves and Gamma-Rays from a Binary Neutron Star Merger: GW170817 and GRB 170817A, The Astrophysical Journal Letters 848, L13, 2017
